question: What risk weights apply to rated corporate exposures under the CRR3 standardised approach?
expected_answer: By ECAI credit quality step: CQS 1 20%, CQS 2 50%, CQS 3 75%, CQS 4 100%, CQS 5 150%, CQS 6 150%.
author: claude-draft

question: What risk weight applies to a corporate exposure without an ECAI credit assessment under the standardised approach?
author: claude-draft

question: What is the maximum total amount owed for an exposure to qualify for the retail exposure class under the standardised approach?
expected_answer: EUR 1 million owed by the obligor or group of connected clients to the institution, its parents and subsidiaries, including defaulted exposures but excluding exposures secured by residential property up to the property value; the exposure must also be to a natural person or SME, part of a significant number of similar exposures, and managed as retail.
author: claude-draft

question: Under the ordinary CRR3 Article 126(1) loan-splitting treatment for an eligible non-IPRE commercial-property exposure, with a sole first lien and no national override, what risk weight applies to the part up to 55% of property value?
expected_answer: 60% for that eligible part. The question assumes the Article 124/126(1) eligibility conditions, a sole first lien and no higher national risk weight or lower national property-value percentage.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27. Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: Required: 60%. Other property branches and junior/pari-passu lien adjustments are optional contextual qualifications.

question: What risk weight does CRR3 assign to land acquisition, development and construction (ADC) exposures under the standardised approach?
expected_answer: 150% (Art. 126a(1)), subject to the exceptions elsewhere in that article.
author: claude-draft

question: What risk weight applies to the unsecured part of a defaulted exposure under the standardised approach?
expected_answer: 150% where specific credit risk adjustments plus Art. 36(1)(m) deductions are less than 20% of the unsecured exposure value (gross of those adjustments); 100% where they are at least 20%.
author: claude-draft

question: Under the fully phased-in general rule in CRR Article 133(3), excluding transitional/grandfathered treatment and the exceptions in paragraphs 4-7 or Part Two, what risk weight applies to equity exposures?
expected_answer: 250% under Article 133(3). This is the end-state general rule, not an assertion of the applicable risk weight for every equity exposure during the Article 495a transition.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27. Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: The question explicitly asks for the end state outside Article 495a and other exceptions. Mentioning transitional treatment is acceptable optional context.

question: How is the exposure value of an on-balance-sheet asset determined under the standardised approach?
expected_answer: Its accounting value after specific credit risk adjustments (Art. 110), additional value adjustments (Art. 34) for non-trading book business, Art. 36(1)(m) deductions and other own funds reductions related to the asset.
author: claude-draft

question: How long must an institution have used rating systems broadly in line with the IRB requirements before it may use the IRB approach?
expected_answer: At least three years prior to qualification for the IRB exposure classes in question; competent authorities assess this experience test under the RTS on IRB assessment methodology.
author: claude-draft

question: When an institution is permitted to use the IRB approach, for how many exposure classes must it implement it at a minimum?
expected_answer: At least one of the exposure classes listed in Art. 148(1), together with its parent and subsidiaries. Once implemented for a type of exposures within an exposure class, it must be implemented for all exposures within that exposure class, unless permanent partial use of the standardised approach is permitted under Art. 150; with prior permission, implementation may be sequential across exposure types, business units, own-LGD use or IRB-CCF.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27 (full passage read). Corrected: 'all exposures within that exposure class', not 'of that type'.

question: Under the general rule in CRR Article 150(1), outside the equity transitional arrangements in Article 495, which approach must an IRB institution use for equity exposures?
expected_answer: The standardised approach for the equity exposure class in Article 147(2)(e), under Article 150(1)(a). This answer is limited to the general rule; it does not deny the separate transitional treatment for previously permitted equity exposures in Article 495.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27. Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: Required: the general SA rule within the stated exclusion. Do not mark a correctly qualified answer about existing transitional permissions wrong. Full Article 495 calculations are not required by this question.

question: For which exposures may an institution use its own IRB conversion factors (IRB-CCF) under CRR3?
expected_answer: With competent-authority permission and compliance with Section 6, IRB-CCF is used for eligible undrawn revolving commitments under IRB that would not have a 100% SA-CCF. Article 151(8) also limits exposure-class eligibility: institution exposures, other financial-sector entities and large corporates outside specialised lending must use SA-CCFs. SA-CCFs also apply to the other off-balance-sheet items, particularly non-revolving undrawn commitments, and where permission or minimum requirements are absent.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27. Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: Required: revolving/non-100%-SA conditions, permission/minimum requirements, and the mandatory-SA exposure-class restriction. Revolving alone is insufficient.

question: What maturity applies under the foundation IRB approach?
expected_answer: Without own-LGD permission, M is either 2.5 years (0.5 years for securities financing transactions) or calculated as for A-IRB under Art. 162(2), applied consistently.
author: claude-draft

question: What is the maximum effective maturity M for exposures under own LGD estimates?
expected_answer: Five years, except the cases in Art. 384(2).
author: claude-draft

question: What is the minimum number of obligor grades for a corporate rating system?
expected_answer: At least 7 grades for non-defaulted obligors and one for defaulted obligors.
author: claude-draft

question: How often must IRB rating assignments of corporate obligors be reviewed, and by whom?
expected_answer: At least annually; assignments and periodic reviews must be completed or approved by an independent party that does not directly benefit from decisions to extend credit.
author: claude-draft

question: When must a corporate exposure be assigned to a facility grade as well as an obligor grade?
expected_answer: When the institution has permission to use own estimates of LGDs and conversion factors; each exposure is then assigned to a facility grade as part of the credit approval process.
author: claude-draft

question: According to the EBA guidelines, which exposures should one rating system cover?
expected_answer: All exposures whose obligors or facilities show common drivers of risk and creditworthiness and fundamentally comparable availability of credit-related information; a PD or LGD model within a rating system may have several calibration segments.
author: claude-draft

question: What does the CRR require once an institution has adjusted its estimates for identified biases?
expected_answer: It must add a sufficient margin of conservatism related to the expected range of estimation errors; the less satisfactory the methods and data, the larger the expected range of errors and the margin.
author: claude-draft

question: How should the observed average default rate be calculated for PD calibration?
expected_answer: As the arithmetic average of all one-year default rates calculated per paras. 73-76; for retail PD models, a weighted average of one-year default rates may be used where the institution does not give equal importance to historic data because more recent data is a better predictor of losses (Art. 180(2)(e) CRR).
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27 (full passage read). Quarantined 2026-11-11: unresolved in source audit; excluded from new frozen benchmark pending current-law/scope adjudication.

question: How must retail PDs be estimated under the CRR?
expected_answer: By obligor or facility grade or pool from long-run averages of one-year default rates; default rates are calculated at facility level only where the default definition is applied at facility level.
author: claude-draft

question: What supervisory LGD values apply under the foundation IRB approach in CRR3?
expected_answer: Senior exposures without eligible funded protection: 45% to central governments, central banks, financial sector entities and regional governments/local authorities/PSEs; 40% to corporates that are not financial sector entities; subordinated exposures without eligible collateral: 75%; eligible covered bonds may receive 11.25%.
author: claude-draft

question: What LGD input floors apply to corporate exposures under own LGD estimates in CRR3?
expected_answer: Unsecured (no eligible funded credit protection): 25%. Fully secured by eligible FCP: financial collateral 0%, receivables 10%, residential or commercial immovable property 10%, other physical collateral 15%.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27 (full passage read).

question: What minimum data period is required for LGD estimates of corporate exposures?
expected_answer: A minimum of five years, increasing by one year each year after implementation until seven years is reached, for at least one data source; a longer available relevant period must be used.
author: claude-draft

question: What LGD must an institution use for exposures already in default?
expected_answer: The sum of its best estimate of expected loss (ELBE) given current economic circumstances and exposure status, and its estimate of the increase in loss rate from possible additional unexpected losses during the recovery period (LGD in-default).
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27. ECB guide (Credit risk) para. 309 accepted as alternative.

question: Which discount rate should be used to calculate realised LGD?
expected_answer: An annual rate equal to the primary interbank offered rate at the moment of default (3-month EURIBOR or a comparable liquid rate in the exposure currency) plus an add-on of 5 percentage points, applied to all recoveries, costs and additional drawings after default.
author: claude-draft

question: Which costs must be included when calculating realised LGDs?
expected_answer: All material direct and indirect costs related to the recovery process. Material collection costs incurred before default are included unless they are already in the outstanding amount at default, or relate to a previous default of the same obligor that is not treated as a multiple default (para. 101).
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27 (full passage read).

question: How should incomplete recovery processes be treated in LGD estimation?
expected_answer: The observed average LGD is adjusted to the long-run average LGD using information on incomplete recovery processes (time since default shorter than the maximum recovery period). For these, institutions must take into account all observed costs and recoveries, and may estimate future costs and recoveries (from collateral and otherwise) within the maximum recovery period.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27 (full passage read).

question: When should the ELBE simply equal the long-run average LGD without adjustment for current economic conditions?
expected_answer: Where any of these holds: (a) the model directly includes at least one macroeconomic risk driver; (b) at least one material risk driver is sensitive to economic conditions; (c) the realised LGD for defaulted exposures is not sensitive to the economic factors relevant for the type of exposures.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27 (full passage read).

question: Which economic indicators must be considered to identify an economic downturn for corporate exposures?
expected_answer: For all exposures: GDP, unemployment rate, externally provided aggregate default rates and credit losses where available; additionally for corporates and retail SMEs: sector- or industry-specific indices (with further indicators for real-estate exposures).
author: claude-draft

question: Over what historical time span must economic indicators be examined to identify a downturn?
expected_answer: 20 years ending when the institution identifies the downturn; a longer span applies where the 20-year variability is not representative.
author: claude-draft

question: Besides back-testing against realised default rates, what validation tools must IRB institutions use?
expected_answer: Other quantitative validation tools and comparisons with relevant external data sources, based on data appropriate to the portfolio, regularly updated and covering a relevant observation period.
author: claude-draft

question: What does the CRR require about changes in validation methods and data over time?
expected_answer: Quantitative validation methods and data must be consistent through time, and changes in estimation and validation methods and data (sources and periods) must be documented.
author: claude-draft

question: What do competent authorities verify when assessing the independence of an IRB validation function?
expected_answer: That the validation unit (or staff) meets all of: (a) independence from the personnel and management functions responsible for originating or renewing exposures and for model design or development; (b) staff different from those designing and developing the rating system and from the credit risk control function; (c) direct reporting to senior management. They also assess whether the chosen organisation of the validation function is adequate (Art. 10(5)).
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27 (full passage read). Corrected: three conditions (a)-(c).

question: What must the management body approve in relation to credit granting under the EBA loan origination guidelines?
expected_answer: Among others: approve the credit risk strategy (aligned with RAF, capital and liquidity planning, ICAAP/ILAAP); set the credit risk appetite incl. credit-granting standards, metrics, limits and escalation thresholds; approve the credit approval framework and delegated authorities; ensure oversight of credit risk quality and provisioning, adequate approval, monitoring and control processes, adequately skilled staff, and the credit risk culture.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27 (full passage read).

question: Under the original 2016 text of EBA/GL/2016/07, before the amendments applying from 19 October 2026, which situations were treated as technical past due and how were they handled?
expected_answer: Only where the defaulted status resulted from: (a) the institution's data or system error (incl. manual errors in standardised processes, not wrong credit decisions); (b) non-, defective or late execution of a payment ordered by the obligor, or payment system failure; (c) a time lag between receipt and allocation of a payment made before day 90; (d) for on-balance factoring, a materiality threshold breach where no receivable is more than 30 days past due. Technical past due situations are not defaults and errors must be rectified as soon as possible.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27 (full passage read). Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: Historical source-comprehension question, not current-law guidance. The registered corpus contains the original 2016 text, whose factoring limb uses 30 days. EBA/GL/2026/05 replaces that limb with a 90-day rule and additional cases; a current-rule answer must not be scored against this historical reference. Remove or replace this question when introducing an updated-current-law-only dataset.

question: Once an obligor meets the past-due criterion, may the bank use expert judgement to avoid default classification?
expected_answer: No: classification is not subject to additional expert judgement and all exposures to the obligor are considered defaulted, unless e.g. the exposures are retail and the default definition is applied at facility level.
author: claude-draft

question: When does an amount become a 'credit obligation past due' for days-past-due counting?
expected_answer: When any amount of principal, interest or fee has not been paid at the date it was due; where the schedule is modified (Art. 178(2)(e)), policies should state that days past due are counted on the modified schedule.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27 (full passage read).

question: What transitional standardised risk weight may be applied to unrated corporates when calculating the output floor?
expected_answer: 65% until 31 December 2032, for corporates without a nominated ECAI assessment whose IRB PD estimate is no greater than 0.5%.
author: claude-draft

question: Which items are eligible financial collateral under all CRM approaches?
expected_answer: Cash on deposit with (or cash-assimilated instruments held by) the lending institution; central government/central bank debt securities rated CQS 1-4; institution and other entities' debt securities rated CQS 1-3; short-term rated debt securities CQS 1-3; equities or convertible bonds in a main index; gold bullion; and non-resecuritisation positions with a risk weight of 100% or lower.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27 (full passage read).

question: What standardised risk weight does an unrated corporate get, and how can that change for output floor purposes?
expected_answer: 100% under Art. 122(2); for the output floor, until end-2032 institutions may instead use 65% if their IRB PD for the obligor is no greater than 0.5% (Art. 465(3)).
author: claude-draft

question: A bank uses F-IRB for a senior unsecured loan to a non-financial large corporate. Which LGD and maturity apply?
expected_answer: Exposures to large corporates must use supervisory LGD values and SA-CCFs (Art. 151(8)(c)): LGD 40% for senior unsecured exposures to non-financial corporates (Art. 161(1)(aa)); M 2.5 years unless calculated under Art. 162(2) (Art. 162(1)).
author: claude-draft

question: How is LGD in-default set for a defaulted retail exposure under own LGD estimates, and when does EBA paragraph 184 require no additional adjustment of the ELBE basis for current economic conditions?
expected_answer: LGD in-default is ELBE plus the estimated increase in loss rate from possible additional unexpected losses during recovery. Under EBA paragraph 184, ELBE is estimated on the long-run average LGD basis without a further current-conditions adjustment where the model directly includes a macroeconomic risk driver, a material risk driver is sensitive to economic conditions, or realised LGD for defaulted exposures is insensitive to the relevant economic factors. The first two cases capture conditions through the model; they do not permit ignoring economic conditions.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27. ECB guide (Credit risk) para. 309 accepted as alternative. Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: No additional adjustment is different from ignoring current conditions. Accept explanations that the model already reflects the cycle.

question: How is an economic downturn period identified for downturn LGD purposes?
expected_answer: Use the relevant indicators by exposure type, including GDP, unemployment and available aggregate default rates/losses, plus appropriate sector/property and other relevant indicators. Examine a 20-year historical window ending at identification, extending it when its variability is not representative of the likely future range. Identify the most severe 12-month indicator values and set a downturn period of at least 12 months, longer where needed to cover related prolonged severity or adjacent peaks/troughs.
author: claude-draft
notes: Checked in source text 2026-10-27. Source audit revision 2026-11-11 (Codex; not practitioner sign-off). Grading criteria and assumptions are in grading_notes.
grading_notes: Required: relevant indicators, the 20-year rule with its representativeness exception, and the minimum rather than fixed 12-month duration.

question: Which elements enter the economic loss when computing realised LGD?
expected_answer: All recoveries, costs and additional drawings after default, discounted at the interbank rate at default (e.g. 3-month EURIBOR) plus 5 percentage points (para. 143), including all material direct and indirect recovery costs (para. 144); economic loss is as defined in Art. 5(2) CRR.
author: claude-draft

question: How is the risk weight of a senior securitisation tranche calculated under SEC-IRBA?
expected_answer: Abstain: securitisation (CRR Part Three Title II Chapter 5) is outside the MVP corpus scope.
author: claude-draft
notes: Tempting: securitisation text is in the full CRR file but outside the MVP article scope.

question: What is the minimum leverage ratio requirement for EU banks?
expected_answer: Abstain: the leverage ratio is outside the credit risk corpus.
author: claude-draft

question: What is the large exposures limit relative to Tier 1 capital?
expected_answer: Abstain: large exposures are outside the credit risk corpus.
author: claude-draft

question: When should a loan move to stage 2 under IFRS 9?
expected_answer: Abstain: IFRS 9 staging is accounting, not in the corpus.
author: claude-draft
notes: The ECB guide and EBA LOM may mention IFRS 9 in passing; the answer should not over-reach.

question: How is the own funds requirement for CVA risk calculated under the basic approach?
expected_answer: Abstain: CVA risk is outside the credit risk corpus.
author: claude-draft
